intro: A backend developer resume built around systems that carry load: what each service does, how much traffic it handles, and what got faster or cheaper.
tips: Name the scale: requests a second, data size, users served.
Show results in latency, cost or reliability, not just the tools used.
Group skills by languages, data stores and infrastructure so they scan fast.

basics.name: Javier Ortega
basics.label: Backend Developer
basics.summary: Backend developer with six years building APIs and data pipelines in Go and Python. I like boring, reliable systems: my last service handled 4,000 requests a second at 99.98% uptime.

work.name: Paymo
highlights: Rebuilt the payouts service in Go; p99 latency fell from 900 ms to 120 ms at 4,000 requests a second.
Moved nightly reconciliation from cron scripts to an event queue, cutting failed payouts by 70%.
Led on-call for a team of five and wrote the runbooks we still use.

work.name: Datalia
highlights: Built the ingestion API in Python (FastAPI) that took 2 billion events a month.
Cut the PostgreSQL bill by 40% by partitioning event tables and archiving to S3.
